title: AuthorityObject
description: Matches governance.authority.AuthorityPolicy.to_authority_object(). Represents one scoped, attributable authority decision or policy grant -- never a bare boolean. Produced by governance/authority.py; documented in docs/governance/AUTHORITY_MODEL.md.

authority_id.description: Unique identifier for this specific (policy, actor) authority object.

actor_id.description: The actor this decision was evaluated for, e.g. 'agent:claude-code-session' or 'human:jamdav688y'.

capability.description: The capability being authorized, e.g. 'PUSH_TAG'. Not a claim of reachability -- see capabilities/registry.json for that, a separate concept.

scope.description: What this decision applies to. 'resource' and 'target' are conventional keys; capability-specific keys (e.g. 'ref_pattern' for git operations) may also appear.

decision.description: See governance.types.AuthorityState. UNKNOWN must never be treated as a synonym for ALLOWED by any consumer of this schema.

constraints.description: Bounds that apply when decision is ALLOWED_BOUNDED. Empty for other decisions. Keys are constraint names (e.g. 'max_amount', 'force_push'); values are the permitted maximum/allow-set.

granted_by.description: Identifier of the policy or authority that produced this object, e.g. a policy_id from governance/policy_defaults.json.

valid_until.description: If set and in the past, the authority is treated as expired -- evaluate_authority() returns UNKNOWN, not the stale decision.

evidence_required.description: Minimum evidence.EvidenceState this capability's promotion/execution should require, if any.

reason.description: Human-readable justification. Every AuthorityDecision must be explainable -- this field is why.
